headings.title: Department administration and rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to administer long-term care provisions and promulgate rules pursuant to chapter 536.

headings.title: Mandatory cooperation of state and local agencies
headings.reviewNote: Directs all state agencies and political subdivisions to cooperate with the department in executing long-term care duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.009 governing department administration, rulemaking authority, and interagency cooperation.

headings.title: Entities exempt from facility licensing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Exempts state or federal facilities, other state-licensed entities, attached chapter 197 hospitals (while retaining specified sections), sections 630.705 to 630.760 facilities, and life care contract providers (except ICF/SNF portions).

headings.title: Voluntary application for licensure by exempt entities
headings.reviewNote: Permits exempt entities to voluntarily apply for licensure under general long-term care statutory provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for section 198.012 governing statutory exemptions from sections 198.003 to 198.136 and voluntary licensure (source notes cross-reference section 42.130 for Missouri veterans homes).

headings.title: License requirement, penalties, and complaint investigations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unlicensed operation as a class A misdemeanor (class E felony if resident abuse or neglect occurred) and mandates complaint investigations within twenty-four hours for abuse/neglect or forty-five days otherwise.

headings.title: Notice of unlicensed operation to prosecutors
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to immediately notify local prosecutors or the attorney general upon identifying unlicensed facilities.

headings.title: Premises restriction and two-year license duration
headings.reviewNote: Limits licenses to named premises and persons and sets license validity for a period of up to two years.

headings.title: Effect of operator ownership changes on license
headings.reviewNote: Requires current operators to notify the department of intent to change operators and succeeding operators to apply for a new license within ten working days of specified partnership or corporate ownership changes.

headings.title: Conspicuous posting of facility license on premises
headings.reviewNote: Mandates posting of facility licenses in conspicuous, public places on the licensed facility premises.

headings.title: Contents of license and authorized resident capacity
headings.reviewNote: Specifies license contents including maximum authorized resident capacity, licensee identities, and expiration dates.

headings.title: License renewal notice and thirty-day application deadline
headings.reviewNote: Requires sixty days advance notice from the department and application submission at least thirty days before expiration.

headings.title: Temporary operating permits during relicensure inspection
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to grant a temporary operating permit for relicensure review and inspection when processing is incomplete prior to expiration through no fault of the operator.

headings.title: Temporary operating permits during operator change evaluations
headings.reviewNote: Directs issuance of temporary operating permits of sufficient duration to evaluate applications resulting from operator changes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsection headings for section 198.015 governing licensing mandates, misdemeanor/felony penalties, complaint investigations, ownership changes, posting, renewals, and mandatory temporary operating permits.

headings.title: License application forms and documentation requirements
headings.reviewNote: Directs operators to submit license applications on forms prescribed by the department with required supporting records.

headings.title: Signed attestation of truth and required documents
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to submit required documents and attest by signature that application statements are true and correct and all required documents are included or on file.

headings.title: License, amendment, and certification fees and quality fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes graduated license fees up to $600, amendment fees up to $50, and annual Medicaid/Medicare certification fees up to $1,000, creating the non-reverting Nursing Facility Quality of Care Fund.

headings.title: Filing replacement or amended documents and daily penalty
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing attested replacement or amended documents within ten working days of their effective date, with circuit court penalties up to $50 per document per day for knowing noncompliance.

headings.title: License revocation or denial for concealment pattern
headings.reviewNote: Makes failure to file required documents or amendments sufficient grounds for license revocation or application disapproval when part of a pattern or practice of concealment.

headings.title: Preemption of local licensing and preserved local inspections
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits political subdivisions from licensing, certifying, or registering state-licensed facilities while preserving authorized county or city food service and fire safety inspections.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for section 198.018 governing license applications, signed attestations, graduated/amendment/certification fees and the Nursing Facility Quality of Care Fund, 10-day amended document filings, concealment revocations, and local licensing preemption.

headings.title: Department review and investigation of applications
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to investigate applications, conduct inspections, and verify operator and controlling person qualifications.

headings.title: Written notice of reasons for license denial
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to notify an applicant in writing of the reasons and grounds upon denying a license application.

headings.title: Facility inspections, record copying, and annual surveys
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes inspections and on-site record copying at department expense within two business days, prohibits removing or disassembling medical records, and mandates at least one unannounced annual inspection.

headings.title: Circuit court order authorizing entry for inspection
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to seek a circuit court entry order when denied access to a suspected unlicensed facility or refused inspection access by a licensed operator.

headings.title: Five-year compliance history for out-of-state applicants
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to request five years of out-of-state facility compliance history when inspecting a facility for an out-of-state operator not previously licensed in Missouri.

headings.title: Accrediting survey reports accepted in lieu of inspection
headings.reviewNote: Permits accepting comparable state, federal, or accrediting agency survey reports for residential care and assisted living facilities, with accreditation posting, abuse forwarding, and full-survey triggers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for section 198.022 governing application review and issuance criteria, written denial notices, facility inspections and record copying, circuit court entry orders, out-of-state compliance history, and acceptance of accrediting survey reports.

headings.title: Notice of noncompliance and deficiency citations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to provide written deficiency notices to facilities following inspections citing specific standards violated.

headings.title: Correction plans, department approval, and reinspections
headings.reviewNote: Establishes five- and ten-working-day plan submission and department review deadlines, immediate class I action, and twenty-day, forty-to-ninety-day, and one-hundred-twenty-day reinspection windows.

headings.title: Issuance of notice of noncompliance after reinspection
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing a notice of noncompliance by dated receipt delivery if a facility remains out of substantial compliance or fails to follow its approved correction plan at reinspection.

headings.title: Notice of potential sanctions and legal remedies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the notice of noncompliance to inform the operator or administrator that the department may seek sanctions and remedies under section 198.067 or other authorized legal action.

headings.title: Consent agreement for probationary license
headings.reviewNote: Allows an operator after inspection to enter a consent agreement for a probationary license with staged compliance deadlines and voluntary license surrender upon noncompliance.

headings.title: Posting and interagency distribution of noncompliance notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires conspicuous facility posting of the noncompliance notice and recent inspection report, and department distribution of the notice to social services, mental health, and concerned agencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for section 198.026 governing inspection exit interviews and correction orders, correction plans and reinspection windows, noncompliance notices, sanction notices, probationary consent agreements, and posting/interagency distribution.

headings.title: Confidentiality of resident medical and personal records
headings.reviewNote: Protects resident medical, financial, and personal records obtained during inspections from public disclosure.

headings.title: Public availability of completed inspection reports
headings.reviewNote: Provides that official inspection reports and statements of deficiencies become open public records after completion.

headings.title: Central registry, hotline caller log, and confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Directs maintenance of a central registry and electronically recorded hotline caller log retained for one year, while keeping the reporter's identity confidential.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for section 198.032 governing confidential resident records, public availability of inspection and complaint reports, and the central registry, hotline caller log, and reporter confidentiality.

headings.title: Statutory grounds for facility license revocation
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates grounds for license revocation including substantial noncompliance, fraud, abuse, and failure to correct deficiencies.

headings.title: Limitation on department access to unnecessary information
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that subdivision (2) of subsection 1 does not authorize department access to information unnecessary to carry out duties under sections 198.006 to 198.186.

headings.title: Written revocation notice and ten-day advance delivery
headings.reviewNote: Requires written revocation notice stating reasons and grounds to be delivered by dated receipt delivery or personal service at least ten days before its effective date.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for section 198.036 governing discretionary license revocation grounds, limits on unnecessary information access, and 10-day written revocation notice (source notes include 1987 Villines v. Division of Aging annotation).

headings.title: Petition to Administrative Hearing Commission for review
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes aggrieved persons to petition the Administrative Hearing Commission within fifteen days of notice of license refusal or revocation without exhausting department remedies.

headings.title: Commission authority to stay revocation on bond
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the commission to stay license revocations pending determination upon conditions including bonds, barring stays for resident danger.

headings.title: Final commission decisions and right to judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Establishes Administrative Hearing Commission determinations as final decisions subject to judicial review by petition in the court of appeals for the district where the facility is located.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for section 198.039 governing 15-day Administrative Hearing Commission petitions, conditional revocation stays, and court of appeals judicial review.

headings.title: State auditor authority to examine facility records
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the state auditor to examine and audit any facility operational records on request or own initiative.

headings.title: Director authority to examine and audit records
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director of the department to examine and audit all operational and financial records of facilities.

headings.title: Seven-year retention requirement for financial records
headings.reviewNote: Requires each facility to retain all financial and operational reimbursement records for at least seven years.

headings.title: Auditor access to facility operational data
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees state auditor access to facility records necessary for conducting statutory audit examinations.

headings.title: Inspection of financial records by legislative committees
headings.reviewNote: Opens financial records upon request to department officials, the state auditor, and appropriate legislative committees.

headings.title: Five-year retention requirement for resident medical records
headings.reviewNote: Mandates retention of resident medical records for five years after discharge, or five years after reaching age twenty-one.

headings.title: Retention of original medical records by successor operator
headings.reviewNote: Requires successor operators taking over facility operations to retain original resident medical records in the facility.

headings.title: Medical record copy required upon resident transfer
headings.reviewNote: Directs that a copy of the resident's medical records accompany the resident whenever transferred from the facility.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.052 governing examination of facility records, financial audits, retention periods, and medical record transfers.

headings.title: Prohibition on offering or advertising unlicensed services
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits offering, advertising, or holding out facility services to the public without a currently valid license.

headings.title: Prohibition against interfering with lawful enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Bars interfering with or preventing department representatives or the attorney general from lawfully enforcing long-term care laws.

headings.title: Criminal penalty classification as class C misdemeanor
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violations of unlicensed advertising or enforcement interference as class C misdemeanors.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.061 governing unlicensed service advertising, enforcement interference, and misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Prohibition on retaining duplicate state agency payments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits operators from retaining duplicate state agency payments exceeding authorized monthly or per diem care rates.

headings.title: Mandatory repayment procedures and monthly interest rate
headings.reviewNote: Directs operators to repay excess amounts with monthly interest at one and five-tenths percent from discovery date.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.064 governing retention of duplicate state payments and repayment interest requirements.

headings.title: Injunctive actions to restrain statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department or attorney general actions in circuit court to enjoin statutory violations or facility admissions.

headings.title: Circuit court actions to recover civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes circuit court civil penalty actions against licensed operators in the county where facilities are located.

headings.title: Daily civil penalty limits and tiered violation amounts
headings.reviewNote: Establishes civil penalty liability up to $25,000 per day with tiered ranges for class I ($1,000–$10,000), class II ($250–$1,000), class III ($50–$250), federal ($250–$500), and doubled repeat violations, plus judgment interest.

headings.title: Civil penalty for false resident assessment certification
headings.reviewNote: Imposes civil penalties up to $1,000 per assessment for willfully certifying a material false statement in a federal resident assessment, or up to $5,000 for causing another individual to do so.

headings.title: Cumulative nature of statutory administrative and judicial remedies
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the imposition of any statutory remedy does not bar the imposition of other legal remedies.

headings.title: Allocation of collected penalties to trust funds
headings.reviewNote: Allocates collected penalties 25% to the elderly home-delivered meals trust fund, 25% to the quality of care fund for ombudsman projects, and 50% to the quality of care fund for department quality programs; sets nonseverable rulemaking (source footnote: word "an" appears in original rolls) and bars charitable tax deductions.

headings.title: Clear and convincing evidence standard of proof
headings.reviewNote: Requires moving parties to prove cited statutory violations by clear and convincing evidence to recover penalties.

headings.title: Confession of judgment by licensed operator
headings.reviewNote: Permits a licensed operator to confess judgment prior to hearing under section 511.070, reducing the recommended civil penalty by twenty-five percent.

headings.title: Reduction of state penalties for federal payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires state penalty amounts reduced by federal monetary penalties paid for the same federal violation events.

headings.title: Enhanced civil penalties for serious injury or abuse
headings.reviewNote: Imposes enhanced penalties up to ten thousand dollars for class I violations causing serious physical injury or abuse.

headings.title: Fine exemption for timely corrected self-reported violations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits fines for self-reported class II and III violations corrected within designated periods without reoccurrence.

headings.title: Non-transferability of civil penalties to successor operators
headings.reviewNote: Provides that assessed civil penalties remain the sole personal liability of the operator at the time of violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 12 subsection headings for section 198.067 governing injunctions, civil penalty actions, tiered daily penalties up to $25,000, false assessment penalties, trust fund allocations (25%/25%/50% and footnote noting word "an" in original rolls), 25% confession-of-judgment reductions, federal offsets, enhanced injury penalties, self-reporting exemptions, and non-transferability.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of resident abuse and neglect
headings.reviewNote: Requires health care workers, coroners, facility staff, and designated professionals to report suspected resident abuse or neglect.

headings.title: Contents of report and sexual assault reporting
headings.reviewNote: Specifies report contents and mandates immediate local law enforcement reporting for suspected sexual assault.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for failure to report abuse
headings.reviewNote: Makes any mandatory reporter who knowingly fails to make a required report within a reasonable time guilty of a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Class E felony for administrator concealing severe abuse
headings.reviewNote: Makes any administrator who knowingly conceals an act of abuse or neglect resulting in death or serious physical injury guilty of a class E felony.

headings.title: Permissive abuse or neglect reporting by other persons
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any other person with reasonable cause to believe a resident has been abused or neglected to report such information to the department.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour investigation, family notice, and referral
headings.reviewNote: Mandates initiating investigations within twenty-four hours, notifying next of kin or responsible parties of the report and findings (unless alleged perpetrator), and reporting substantiated elder abuse to law enforcement and prosecutors.

headings.title: Director referral and court petition for resident removal
headings.reviewNote: Directs investigator referral to the director and authorizes circuit court petitions and ex parte orders for up to thirty days of temporary care and protection when immediate removal is necessary.

headings.title: Confidentiality of abuse and neglect reports
headings.reviewNote: Provides that abuse and neglect reports shall be confidential pursuant to section 192.2500.

headings.title: Statutory immunity for good faith abuse reports
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from civil and criminal liability to persons reporting abuse or participating in proceedings in good faith.

headings.title: Five-working-day written notice to mandatory reporter
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notification to the reporter within five working days of receiving a required report confirming receipt and initiation of investigation.

headings.title: Prohibition against retaliation and information contact line
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits facility authorities from evicting, harassing, dismissing, or retaliating against reporting residents or employees, and provides rights information through the department contact line.

headings.title: Criminal prosecution for resident abuse or neglect
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any person who abuses or neglects a facility resident to criminal prosecution under section 565.184.

headings.title: Employee disqualification list and culpability definitions
headings.reviewNote: Requires placing employees finally determined to have knowingly or recklessly abused or neglected a resident on the employee disqualification list and defines "knowingly" and "recklessly".

headings.title: Investigation and classification of self-reported incidents
headings.reviewNote: Requires investigating timely facility self-reports to the central registry as self-reported incidents rather than hotline calls, reporting them as substantiated if a regulatory violation results.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 14 subsection headings for section 198.070 governing mandatory/permissive abuse reporting, sexual assault reports, failure-to-report and concealment penalties, 24-hour investigations, court removal petitions, confidentiality, immunity, 5-day notices, anti-retaliation, criminal prosecution, employee disqualification list, and self-reported incidents (source notes include 1989 State v. Dale annotations).

headings.title: Eligibility criteria for residential care facility placement
headings.reviewNote: Limits residential care placement to individuals capable of self-preservation and mental competence under emergency conditions.

headings.title: Forty-five-day temporary incapacity retention with approval
headings.reviewNote: Permits previously qualified residents with temporary incapacity up to forty-five days from illness, surgery, or injury to remain in a residential care or assisted living facility with physician approval.

headings.title: Grandfathered residential care II assisted living licensure
headings.reviewNote: Grants assisted living licensure on August 28, 2006 to residential care II facilities meeting August 27, 2006 rules until Medicaid reimbursement reaches $41/day, while barring noncompliant evacuation-impaired care.

headings.title: Assisted living admission, service plan, and retention rules
headings.reviewNote: Establishes contract, 24-hour staffing, disaster plan, pre-move-in screening, semiannual assessment, individualized service plan, restraint, and retention-bar standards for assisted living facilities.

headings.title: Hospice exception to assisted living retention prohibitions
headings.reviewNote: Requires exceptions to specified assisted living retention bars for hospice residents when the resident or representative, provider, physician, and licensed hospice provider all agree.

headings.title: Requirements for residents unable to evacuate with minimal aid
headings.reviewNote: Requires awake 24-hour staff, individualized evacuation plans, facility exploration opportunities, and physician-recommended personal electronic monitoring for evacuation-impaired assisted living residents.

headings.title: Admission physical examination and hospital transfer exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires a licensed physician admission physical examination on file within ten days of admission, exempting direct transfers from hospitals or long-term care facilities accompanied by current medical reports.

headings.title: Mandatory pre-admission disclosures by assisted living facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires assisted living facilities to disclose available or coordinated services, costs, and conditions requiring discharge or transfer to prospective residents or legal representatives.

headings.title: Restrictions on advertising as an assisted living facility
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unlicensed assisted living advertising after January 1, 2008 and restricts residential care II use of the term after August 28, 2006, with an exception for pre-August 28, 2006 social-model intermediate care facilities.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs department rulemaking to ensure compliance with section 198.073 subject to chapter 536, section 536.028, and post-August 28, 2006 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 10 subsection headings for section 198.073 governing residential care eligibility, 45-day temporary incapacity, grandfathered residential care II licensure, assisted living admission/retention rules, hospice exceptions, evacuation-impaired care, admission physicals, disclosures, advertising limits, and nonseverable rulemaking.

headings.title: NFPA 13 sprinklers for new and renovated facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires new facilities licensed or sections completing major renovations on or after August 28, 2007 to install and maintain an NFPA 13 sprinkler system.

headings.title: Grandfathered maintenance for pre-August 2007 sprinklers
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities initially licensed with an approved sprinkler system before August 28, 2007 to continue meeting August 27, 2007 testing, inspection, and maintenance rules.

headings.title: Sprinkler standards for assisted living evacuation impairments
headings.reviewNote: Requires NFPA 13 sprinklers in multi-level and NFPA 13R sprinklers in single-story assisted living facilities accepting or retaining residents unable to safely evacuate with minimal assistance.

headings.title: 2012 sprinkler deadline for larger residential and assisted care
headings.reviewNote: Requires pre-August 28, 2007 residential care and assisted living facilities with over twenty residents to install NFPA 13R or 13 sprinklers by December 31, 2012, unless meeting NFPA 101 Chapter 33.

headings.title: 2012 NFPA 13 deadline and water-supply exemption for nursing
headings.reviewNote: Requires skilled nursing and intermediate care facilities not previously required to have sprinklers to install NFPA 13 systems by December 31, 2012, unless exempted for documented water supply unavailability.

headings.title: Sprinkler loan eligibility, 2013 deadline, and repayment terms
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes state treasurer loans under section 198.075 (subject to a $52/day Medicaid threshold by December 31, 2009), sets a December 31, 2013 NFPA 13 fallback deadline, and ties 5-, 8-, and 10-year repayment terms to Medicaid rates.

headings.title: Fire alarm systems, smoke partitions, and 2008 enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Mandates complete NFPA 101 or NFPA 72 fire alarm systems, interim smoke alarms and heat detectors, one-hour rated smoke partitions (with a 75-foot exemption), enforceable December 31, 2008.

headings.title: Supersession of section 198.058 construction exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that section 198.074 requirements supersede the construction-standard exemptions in section 198.058.

headings.title: Annual fire safety inspections by department and fire marshal
headings.reviewNote: Assigns annual fire safety inspections to the department for skilled nursing and intermediate care facilities (with inspector training by December 31, 2012) and to the state fire marshal for residential care and assisted living.

headings.title: July 1, 2008 deadline to submit compliance plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires all licensed facilities to submit a compliance plan for section 198.074 to the state fire marshal by July 1, 2008.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 10 subsection headings for section 198.074 governing NFPA 13/13R sprinkler mandates, pre-2007 grandfathering, 2012/2013 deadlines, water-supply exemptions, state treasurer loans, NFPA 101/72 fire alarms and smoke partitions, section 198.058 supersession, annual inspections, and 2008 compliance plans.

headings.title: Establishment of Fire Safety Standards Loan Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Fire Safety Standards Loan Fund in the state treasury with the state treasurer as custodian, credits investment earnings to the fund, and provides that moneys remaining at biennium end revert to general revenue.

headings.title: State treasurer loan applications and qualifying facilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs qualifying facilities in substantial compliance with no uncorrected deficiencies to apply for loans to the state treasurer's office for review prior to allocation.

headings.title: Maximum two and one-half percent loan interest rate
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the fund shall be a loan with an interest rate not exceeding two and one-half percent.

headings.title: Administration of loan fund by state treasurer's office
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the Fire Safety Standards Loan Fund shall be administered by the state treasurer's office.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for section 198.075 governing the Fire Safety Standards Loan Fund (with biennial reversion to general revenue), state treasurer loan applications, the 2.5% interest cap, and state treasurer administration.

headings.title: Mandatory nursing assistant training and certification
headings.reviewNote: Requires nursing assistants employed in facilities to complete approved training and achieve state certification.

headings.title: Definition of certified nursing assistant
headings.reviewNote: Defines "certified nursing assistant" as an employee who completed required training, passed the certification exam, and provides direct resident health care under a chapter 335 licensed nurse.

headings.title: Exemptions for licensed personnel and unpaid volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts state-regulated or licensed health care personnel and uncompensated volunteers or religious or fraternal order members operating the facility.

headings.title: Classroom and supervised on-the-job training hour minimums
headings.reviewNote: Requires regulatory training standards of at least seventy-five classroom hours and one hundred supervised on-the-job hours completed within four months of employment.

headings.title: Direct nurse supervision before completing classroom hours
headings.reviewNote: Permits nursing assistants who have not completed training before employment to provide direct resident care only under a licensed nurse's direct supervision until finishing seventy-five classroom hours.

headings.title: Facility or comparable laboratory competency evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Requires performing the competency evaluation in a facility under 42 CFR 483.5 or a comparable laboratory setting.

headings.title: Exam eligibility for unlicensed assistive personnel trainees
headings.reviewNote: Allows persons completing unlicensed assistive personnel training under 19 CSR 30-20.125 and competency evaluation to sit for the CNA exam and satisfy classroom and clinical standards.

headings.title: Additional department training programs and certifications
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to offer additional training programs and certifications to already certified nursing assistants under department regulations and board-approved curriculum.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsection headings for section 198.082 governing CNA training programs, statutory definition, licensed/volunteer exemptions, 75-classroom/100-on-the-job hour minimums, direct supervision, competency evaluations, UAP exam eligibility, and additional department training.

headings.title: Facility duty to establish resident rights policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to adopt and enforce written policies guaranteeing fundamental resident rights and personal dignity.

headings.title: Civil and religious liberties, rights statement, and training
headings.reviewNote: Directs facilities and the department to support civil and religious liberties, provide each resident a statement of rights and facility rules, and implement a written rights-and-privacy plan with staff training.

headings.title: Facility and department resident grievance procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires department-approved facility grievance procedures, a full-time staff designee, 14-day filing and 3-day written response timelines, and department complaint review and referral rules.

headings.title: Referral of licensed professional violations to boards
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to forward investigative findings of violations by licensees under chapters 330–338 or 344 to the appropriate licensing or examining board.

headings.title: Maintenance and inspection of complaint disposition records
headings.reviewNote: Requires each facility to maintain a complete record of complaints, grievances, and final dispositions open to department inspection during normal business hours.

headings.title: No exhaustion required before section 198.090 complaint
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that residents are not required to exhaust facility or department grievance procedures before filing a complaint under section 198.090.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for section 198.088 governing facility policies and resident rights, civil/religious liberties and staff training, facility and department grievance procedures, board referrals, complaint disposition records, and non-exhaustion for section 198.090 complaints.

headings.title: Holding resident personal property and funds in trust
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes facilities to hold resident personal funds in trust only upon written authorization from residents or guardians.

headings.title: Written receipt statements for gifts of ten dollars or more
headings.reviewNote: Requires owners, operators, managers, employees, or affiliates receiving property worth $10 or more from a resident to make an inspectable written statement, with failure a class C misdemeanor.

headings.title: One-hundred-dollar annual limit on gifts from residents
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any owner, operator, manager, employee, or affiliate from receiving personal property or things of value totaling over $100 from facility residents in one calendar year.

headings.title: Exemptions for trust funds, contracts, and close relatives
headings.reviewNote: Exempts property held in trust under subsection 1, received under a lawful contract or for services rendered, or received from a resident related within the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity.

headings.title: Class C misdemeanor for failing to keep separate accounts
headings.reviewNote: Makes an operator's failure to maintain required records or keep resident personal funds in an account separate from facility funds a class C misdemeanor.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for diverting resident personal funds
headings.reviewNote: Makes an operator, affiliate, or employee who puts resident personal funds to personal or facility use or diverts them guilty of a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Permissive reporting of suspected fund misappropriation
headings.reviewNote: Permits any person with reasonable cause to believe a resident's funds or property have been misappropriated to report the information to the department.

headings.title: Information division attempts to obtain for each report
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to attempt to obtain facility, employee, resident, and complainant names, misappropriation details, and other helpful investigative information.

headings.title: Mandatory department investigation upon receiving report
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to initiate an investigation upon receipt of a misappropriation report.

headings.title: Referral of probable misappropriation to department director
headings.reviewNote: Directs the investigator to refer the complaint and report to the department director or designee when investigation indicates probable misappropriation.

headings.title: Confidentiality of misappropriation reports
headings.reviewNote: Provides that misappropriation reports shall be confidential under section 192.2500.

headings.title: Immunity for good-faith reporters and testifying witnesses
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and criminal immunity (except perjury, negligence, recklessness, bad faith, or malice) to reporters and witnesses not participating in or benefiting from the misappropriation.

headings.title: Five-working-day written notice of report receipt
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notification to the reporter within five working days of receiving a required report confirming receipt and initiation of investigation.

headings.title: Prohibition against retaliation for reporting violations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits facility authorities from evicting, harassing, dismissing, or retaliating against a resident or employee for reporting suspected legal or regulatory violations.

headings.title: Employee disqualification list for misappropriation
headings.reviewNote: Requires placing employees finally determined under section 192.2490 to have misappropriated resident property or funds on the employee disqualification list.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 15 subsection headings for section 198.090 governing resident trust funds, $10 gift statements and $100 annual limits, exemptions, separate-account and diversion misdemeanors, misappropriation reporting, investigations, confidentiality, immunity, 5-day notices, anti-retaliation, and the employee disqualification list.

headings.title: Written complaint to attorney general for rights deprivation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes residents or estates to file written complaints with the attorney general within one hundred eighty days of violation.

headings.title: Attorney general review and initiation of legal actions
headings.reviewNote: Directs the attorney general to review complaints and authorizes initiating civil enforcement actions under long-term care laws.

headings.title: Private civil action following attorney general inaction
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes private civil damage suits against owners or operators within two hundred forty days if the attorney general does not sue.

headings.title: Affirmative defense of reasonable care by owner
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an affirmative defense for owners or operators proving they exercised all reasonably necessary preventative care.

headings.title: Exemption for actions recovering on personal funds bond
headings.reviewNote: Exempts actions against personal funds surety bonds under section 198.096 from prior attorney general complaint requirements.

headings.title: Preservation of common law and statutory legal remedies
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that statutory rights remedies do not abrogate or limit independent common law or statutory rights of action.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.093 governing complaints for resident rights violations, attorney general reviews, and civil suits.

headings.title: Mandatory surety bond for resident trust funds
headings.reviewNote: Requires operators holding resident funds in trust to file a surety bond equal to one and one-half times monthly balances.

headings.title: Bond condition securing return of resident property
headings.reviewNote: Conditions surety bonds to secure full return of trust moneys wrongfully deprived by operators, affiliates, or employees.

headings.title: Director authority to require increased bond amounts
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to require increased bond amounts whenever existing bonds are deemed insufficient or impaired.

headings.title: Sixty days advance notice required for bond cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that bond cancellation provisions require sureties to provide at least sixty days advance notice to the department.

headings.title: Cash deposit in escrow in lieu of bond
headings.reviewNote: Permits operators to establish cash deposits in noncancelable insured bank escrows in lieu of corporate surety bonds.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.096 governing personal funds surety bonds, bond amounts, impairment, and escrow accounts.

headings.title: Misappropriation of resident funds as class E felony
headings.reviewNote: Makes managing financial affairs of elderly residents and misappropriating funds needed for care a class E felony.

headings.title: Certified mail notice as evidence of care nonpayment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that certified mail notices of unpaid care expenses constitute admissible evidence of care nonpayment.

headings.title: Preservation of financial exploitation prosecutions
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that statutory provisions do not limit investigations or prosecutions for financial exploitation under section 570.145.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.097 governing criminal misappropriation of resident funds, class E felony, and notice proof.

headings.title: Verified petition for appointment of facility receiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires verified petitions supported by affidavits showing statutory emergency conditions filed in Cole County or facility circuit courts.

headings.title: Court appointment of receiver from department list
headings.reviewNote: Directs circuit courts to appoint qualified receivers upon finding statutory grounds and necessity for resident protection.

headings.title: Maintenance of qualified receiver list by department
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department director to maintain an official list of qualified individuals requesting receiver appointments.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.105 governing receivership petitions, court appointment of receivers, and qualification lists.

headings.title: Receiver avoidance of unconscionable executory contracts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes receivers to avoid honoring unconscionable leases, mortgages, or executory contracts entered into by prior operators.

headings.title: Court application to determine reasonable rental payments
headings.reviewNote: Permits receivers to apply to court for setting reasonable rental rates for essential leased real estate or property.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.115 governing avoidance of unconscionable executory contracts and reasonable rental settings.

headings.title: Receiver duty to render complete court accounting
headings.reviewNote: Requires receivers to provide complete financial accountings of property, collections, and expenses within thirty days of termination.

headings.title: Distribution of surplus funds or operator liability
headings.reviewNote: Directs payment of surplus funds to operators and establishes operator liability for reasonable expense deficiencies.

headings.title: Judicial determination and entry of deficiency judgment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes receivers to petition courts for deficiency determinations and judgments against operators after notice and hearing.

headings.title: Assignment of deficiency judgments upon court approval
headings.reviewNote: Permits receivers to assign deficiency judgments in whole or in part upon obtaining circuit court approval.

headings.title: Priority of receivership deficiency judgment liens
headings.reviewNote: Establishes priority for deficiency judgments over other subsequent liens, excepting approved mechanic's liens.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.132 governing receiver accounting, operating surplus, deficiency judgments, and lien priority.

headings.title: Prohibition of false statements for Medicaid certification
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits health care providers from knowingly making material false statements to qualify for initial or recertified Medicaid funding.

headings.title: Prohibition on inducing false statements for consideration
headings.reviewNote: Bars health care providers from knowingly inducing false statements or representations of material fact for direct or indirect consideration.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.155 governing prohibitions against false statements in Medicaid certification and consideration.

headings.title: Criminal classification of Medicaid fraud as felony
headings.reviewNote: Classifies criminal violations of health care provider fraud sections as class E felonies.

headings.title: Mandatory disqualification from receiving future Medicaid funds
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits convicted providers from receiving future Medicaid payments, permitting discretionary department reinstatement.

headings.title: Civil liability to state for moneys obtained under Medicaid
headings.reviewNote: Holds a vendor or health care provider violating sections 198.139 to 198.155 civilly liable to the state for any moneys obtained under Medicaid as a result of such act or omission.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for section 198.158 governing class E felony Medicaid fraud penalties, Medicaid disqualification and reinstatement review, and civil liability for moneys obtained under Medicaid.

headings.title: Establishment of Fraud Investigation Division in department
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Fraud Investigation Division within the department of social services headed by a division director.

headings.title: Director authority to investigate provider fraud
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the division director to investigate allegations of Medicaid fraud and enforce health care provider accountability laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.161 governing the Fraud Investigation Division, appointment of director, and legal authority.

headings.title: Withholding of Medicaid payments during fraud investigations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the fraud investigation division director, upon probable cause of a violation of sections 198.139 to 198.186, to petition a court for an order stopping Medicaid payments pending investigation and litigation.

headings.title: Court hearing and written decision on stopping payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to allow the health care provider an opportunity to be heard on the director's request and to decide in writing whether to stop payments.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for section 198.165 governing court petitions to stop Medicaid payments during fraud investigations and provider hearing and written court decision requirements.

headings.title: Director authority to conduct investigative hearings
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the fraud division director to conduct investigative hearings, administer oaths, and subpoena witnesses and documents.

headings.title: Circuit court enforcement of administrative subpoenas
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes applying to circuit courts for orders compelling obedience to subpoenas under penalty of contempt.

headings.title: Accountant-client privilege waiver in fraud proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Provides that accountant-client privileges do not apply to subpoenas upon knowing waiver by persons subject to regulation.

headings.title: Confidentiality of records and restricted litigation disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Restricts disclosure of investigative records except in civil or criminal litigation, or to prosecutorial and department agencies.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalty for improper record disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Classifies improper disclosure of confidential fraud investigation records as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Supplementary nature of investigative statutory powers
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that fraud investigation powers do not repeal existing statutes and operate as supplementary authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.174 governing investigative hearings, subpoenas, accountant privilege waiver, and confidentiality.

headings.title: Compulsion of testimony and grant of immunity
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes courts to compel testimony and grant immunity against criminal self-incrimination in fraud proceedings.

headings.title: Judicial contempt finding for refusal to testify
headings.reviewNote: Empowers courts to find witnesses in contempt for continuing to refuse to testify after receiving immunity.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.177 governing compulsion of testimony, grants of immunity, and contempt sanctions.

headings.title: State agency and law enforcement duty to cooperate
headings.reviewNote: Directs all state agencies and law enforcement officers to assist and cooperate with the fraud investigation division.

headings.title: Department duty to refer substantial fraud complaints
headings.reviewNote: Requires department divisions to promptly notify and refer substantial complaints of provider fraud to the division director.

headings.title: Division access to department records and Medicaid data
headings.reviewNote: Mandates complete division access to department Medicaid records and requires electronic data processing support.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.183 governing interagency cooperation with the fraud division, referrals, and electronic access.

headings.title: Creation and territorial boundaries of nursing home districts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes creation and management of nursing home districts including municipal and unincorporated territories in one or more counties.

headings.title: Corporate status, district naming, and taxing powers
headings.reviewNote: Designates organized districts as political subdivisions with corporate powers to sue, be sued, and levy authorized taxes.

headings.title: Definition of nursing home for district statutes
headings.reviewNote: Defines nursing home for district provisions to include licensed residential care, assisted living, intermediate, and skilled facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.200 governing nursing home district creation, corporate status, and statutory definitions.

headings.title: County commission hearing on district formation petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires county clerks to present petitions to county commissioners who shall schedule public hearings within thirty to forty days.

headings.title: Publication and posting of public hearing notices
headings.reviewNote: Directs notice by publication on three separate days in general circulation newspapers at least twenty days before the hearing, or posting in ten of the most public places if no such newspaper exists.

headings.title: Advance payment and tax reimbursement of notice costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires petitioners to advance notice publication expenses, reimbursable from district tax receipts upon successful organization.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.220 governing county commission hearing notices on petitions and advance publication costs.

headings.title: Election districts or at-large board, terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Directs the county commission either to divide the district into six equal election districts or elect six at-large directors within ninety days, and sets three-year terms and board vacancy-filling rules.

headings.title: Circuit court option for at-large board elections
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes circuit courts following initial elections to choose electing the board of directors on an at-large basis.

headings.title: Director qualifications and candidacy declaration filings
headings.reviewNote: Requires director candidates to be U.S. citizens, resident taxpayers with one year of state residency, and at least twenty-four years old, filing declarations with the county commission at least twenty days before the special election.

headings.title: Assumption of office when board candidates are uncontested
headings.reviewNote: Provides that if candidates equal the number of seats to be elected, no election is held and candidates assume office.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.280 governing board election districts, director qualifications, declarations, and uncontested races.

headings.title: Board executive powers, initial meeting, and officers
headings.reviewNote: Vests legislative and executive powers in the board, requiring a first meeting within thirty days to elect a chairman, select a secretary and treasurer, define fiscal years, and adopt a seal and bylaws.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and faithful discharge of duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires directors to devote necessary time to duties and mandates that directors serve without financial compensation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.290 governing board powers, initial meetings, officer selection, and uncompensated service.

headings.title: General governmental and operational powers of district
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates district powers including facility construction, maintenance, condemnation, leasing, borrowing, and healthcare staffing.

headings.title: Board regulation and control of facility use
headings.reviewNote: Subjects nursing home facility usage to reasonable regulations and terms established by the district board of directors.

headings.title: Suspension or revocation of privileges for violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes regulatory ordinances providing for suspension or revocation of district privileges for ordinance violations.

headings.title: State statutory and regulatory supremacy over district rules
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits district regulations conflicting with state health laws or diminishing state licensing standards under sections 198.003 to 198.096.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.300 governing nursing home district powers, facility regulations, penalties, and state law supremacy.

headings.title: Board determination to sell unsuitable facility site
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes boards to sell unsuitable or unnecessary nursing home property upon adopting resolutions setting forth sale reasons.

headings.title: County commission approval of resolution and deed execution
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing a certified copy of the board's sale resolution with the county clerk for county commission approval by order of record, after which the board may sell and the board secretary executes the deed.

headings.title: Disposition and use of property sale proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Directs remaining sale proceeds deposited into the district treasury to finance new site acquisitions or district purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for section 198.305 governing board resolutions to sell unsuitable facility sites, county commission approval and deed execution, and disposition of sale proceeds.

headings.title: Board authority to incur indebtedness and issue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes boards to borrow money and issue general obligation bonds for purchasing sites and constructing nursing homes.

headings.title: Statutory ballot form for nursing home bond question
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the substantially standard ballot wording for submitting a nursing home district borrowing and bond question to voters.

headings.title: Board authority to borrow upon constitutional voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Vests the board with power to borrow money and issue bonds for the ballot amount and purposes if approved by the constitutionally required percentage of votes, subject to subsection 4.

headings.title: Twenty-year limit, ten-percent debt cap, and tax levy
headings.reviewNote: Limits loans to twenty years and aggregate debt to ten percent of taxable tangible property valuation, caps interest at the legal contract rate, and mandates an annual interest and sinking-fund tax.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for section 198.310 governing nursing home district borrowing authority, ballot form, constitutional voter approval, and 20-year term, 10% debt cap, and tax levy rules.

headings.title: Revenue bond terms, maximum interest, and call provisions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes serial or term revenue bonds in board-determined denominations, maturities, legal interest rates, and optional prior-redemption call and premium terms.

headings.title: Negotiable instrument status and state tax exemption
headings.reviewNote: Declares revenue bonds negotiable instruments under commercial law and exempts interest from Missouri state income taxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.316 governing revenue bonds, terms, negotiable instrument status, and income tax exemptions.

headings.title: Board covenants securing revenue bond debt service
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to prescribe revenue bond form, details, and incidents and make advisable covenants to secure payment consistent with sections 198.312 to 198.318.

headings.title: Bondholder civil remedies at law or in equity
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes bondholders or coupon holders to bring civil actions at law or in equity to compel board performance of statutory duties and bond covenants.

headings.title: Revenue bonds as alternative nonexclusive financing method
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that revenue bond provisions are nonexclusive alternative methods of financing nursing home district facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.318 governing revenue bond covenants, bondholder remedies, and alternative financing methods.

headings.title: Voter petition for annexation of contiguous territory
headings.reviewNote: Requires annexation petitions signed by ten percent or fifty registered voters residing in proposed annexation areas.

headings.title: Standard statutory ballot form for annexation election
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the standard ballot question submitted to voters regarding annexation to the nursing home district.

headings.title: Dual majority vote required to approve annexation
headings.reviewNote: Requires separate majority voter approvals in both the existing district and proposed territory to effectuate annexation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.320 governing annexation of territory to nursing home districts, voter petitions, and ballot approvals.

headings.title: Nursing facility reimbursement allowance payment obligation
headings.reviewNote: Requires nursing facilities, except state-operated facilities, to pay reimbursement allowances for the privilege of operating.

headings.title: Definition of engaging in nursing facility business
headings.reviewNote: Defines engaging in the business of providing nursing services as accepting payments for providing care in Missouri.

headings.title: Definition of nursing facility and federal qualification
headings.reviewNote: Defines nursing facility under federal Medicaid law, qualifying as a distinct provider class under Public Law 102-234.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for section 198.401 governing nursing facility reimbursement allowance obligations, business definition, and federal class qualification (source notes: expires 9-30-29 per section 198.439).

headings.title: Facility records and annual October report transmittal
headings.reviewNote: Requires nursing facilities to maintain records and submit annual cost statements to social services on or before October first.

headings.title: Department determinations absent desk-reviewed cost reports
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to determine allowance elements by rule if facilities lack third prior year desk-reviewed reports.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for section 198.406 governing facility records, October first annual transmittals, and department determinations absent desk-reviewed cost reports (source notes: expires 9-30-29 per section 198.439).

headings.title: Director determination of reimbursement allowance amount
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director of social services to determine the annual reimbursement allowance due from each nursing facility.

headings.title: Annual notification of allowance and monthly installment payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual allowance notification by October first and permits payment in monthly* increments over the balance of the period (source footnote: word "month" appears in original rolls).

headings.title: Voluntary offset of allowance against state payments
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department to offset reimbursement allowances against Medicaid payments owed to facilities upon facility request.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for section 198.409 governing allowance determinations, October first notices and monthly* installments (footnote: word "month" appears in original rolls), and voluntary payment offsets (source notes: expires 9-30-29 per section 198.439).

headings.title: Finality of allowance determination absent timely protest
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that reimbursement allowance determinations are final unless facilities file written protests setting forth grounds.

headings.title: Department reconsideration and forty-five day hearing deadline
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to reconsider determinations upon protest and schedule administrative hearings within forty-five days.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for section 198.412 governing 30-day determination finality and protests, 45-day reconsideration hearings, and Administrative Hearing Commission appeals (source notes: expires 9-30-29 per section 198.439).

headings.title: Remittance of reimbursement allowance to department
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to remit reimbursement allowance amounts or net balances payable to the director of revenue.

headings.title: Offset or fund payment satisfies statutory obligation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that requested state payment offsets or direct fund payments satisfy facility reimbursement allowance obligations under section 198.401.

headings.title: Treasurer maintenance and disclosure of fund balances
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state treasurer to maintain accounting records of fund balances and investment earnings, disclosed upon request.

headings.title: Exemption of fund balance from biennial reversion
headings.reviewNote: Exempts unexpended balances in the reimbursement allowance fund from lapsing into the general revenue fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for section 198.418 governing allowance remittances and fund creation, obligation satisfaction, treasurer balance records, and biennial nonreversion (source notes: expires 9-30-29 per section 198.439).

headings.title: Annual reimbursement allowance period and balance notices
headings.reviewNote: Defines the annual allowance period from October first through September thirtieth, requiring annual notices of balances due.

headings.title: Enforcement of state lien for delinquent allowances
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes social services to enforce state tax liens against facility property for unpaid delinquent reimbursement allowances.

headings.title: License denial or revocation for delinquent allowances
headings.reviewNote: Establishes delinquent reimbursement allowances as grounds for denying, suspending, or revoking facility operating licenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for section 198.421 governing annual allowance periods and delinquency, state lien enforcement and Medicaid provider cancellation, and license sanctions (source notes: expires 9-30-29 per section 198.439).

headings.title: Mandatory disclosure for Alzheimer's special care units
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities offering Alzheimer's care units to disclose distinguishing care forms, philosophies, and programming.

headings.title: Standardized disclosure form developed by department
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to develop standardized disclosure forms detailing admission criteria, staffing, and specialized therapies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.510 governing disclosure requirements for Alzheimer's special care units and standardized forms.

headings.title: Department duty to inspect licensed care facilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of health and senior services to inspect all licensed residential and nursing care facilities.

headings.title: Two-year employment restriction on assigning surveyors
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits assigning surveyors to inspect facilities where they were employed within the preceding two years.

headings.title: Surveyor disclosure of affiliations and family ties
headings.reviewNote: Requires newly hired and existing surveyors to disclose past employment, affiliations, and immediate family connections.

headings.title: Definition of immediate family member
headings.reviewNote: Defines immediate family member for surveyor conflict-of-interest restrictions to include spouses, children, parents, and siblings.

headings.title: Public record status of surveyor disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Designates surveyor disclosure statements as open public records under chapter 610 sunshine law provisions.

headings.title: Public notification of surveyor conflicts of interest
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any person to notify the department of facts demonstrating surveyor affiliations creating conflicts of interest.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.525 governing long-term care facility inspections, surveyor conflict-of-interest bans, and disclosures.

headings.title: Mandatory annual unannounced inspection of facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to inspect all licensed facilities at least once annually without prior notice during day or night.

headings.title: Annual department re-evaluation of inspection process
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to conduct annual re-evaluations of the inspection process to ensure statutory compliance.

headings.title: Need-to-know disclosure and penalty for advance notice
headings.reviewNote: Restricts unannounced survey schedules to need-to-know employees and punishes advance disclosure as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.526 governing mandatory unannounced annual inspections and confidentiality of survey schedules.

headings.title: Website publication of facility surveys and deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to publish recent survey findings, deficiency severity ratings, and inspection history on its website.

headings.title: Protection of protected health information under HIPAA
headings.reviewNote: Exempts protected health information from website publication in compliance with federal HIPAA privacy regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.528 governing department website posting of facility inspection surveys and HIPAA protections.

headings.title: Managed care option for facility resident enrollees
headings.reviewNote: Requires managed care organizations to provide enrollees the option of receiving postacute care in their resident facility.

headings.title: Medicare allowable rate for facility reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Directs managed care organizations to reimburse resident facilities at rates not less than the Medicare allowable rate.

headings.title: Scope of covered postacute and therapy services
headings.reviewNote: Specifies covered services including skilled nursing, rehabilitative therapies, and postacute medical care.

headings.title: Protection of health carrier participating provider access
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits facilities from barring network providers or charging enrollees ancillary fees for covered services.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.530 governing managed care options in resident facilities, reimbursement, and provider access.

headings.title: Thirty-day deadline for investigating resident harm complaints
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to investigate complaints alleging resident harm or imminent harm within thirty days of receipt.

headings.title: Written disclosure of investigation results to parties
headings.reviewNote: Directs written disclosure of investigation findings to complainants, facilities, residents, and family members upon request.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.532 governing investigation of facility complaints alleging harm and written report disclosures.

headings.title: Citation as Missouri Informal Dispute Resolution Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates section 198.545 as the Missouri Informal Dispute Resolution Act.

headings.title: Definitions for informal dispute resolution provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines deficiency, department, facility, IDR, and quality improvement organization for dispute proceedings.

headings.title: Independent third-party contract for dispute resolution
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to contract with an independent quality improvement organization to conduct informal dispute resolution.

headings.title: Establishment of IDR process for cited deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Directs establishment of an informal administrative conference process incorporating federal dispute standards under 42 CFR 488.331.

headings.title: Ten-day deadline for independent organization determination
headings.reviewNote: Requires the review organization to issue its written determination and findings within ten days of the IDR conference.

headings.title: Department review and rationale for reversing determinations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to transmit its rationale within ten calendar days if it reverses the independent determination.

headings.title: Issuance of revised statement of cited deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to issue revised deficiency statements within ten days when original citations are modified.

headings.title: Ten-day deadline for submitting plan of correction
headings.reviewNote: Directs facilities to submit plans of correction within ten calendar days of receiving final dispute determinations.

headings.title: Prohibition on posting disputed deficiencies pending resolution
headings.reviewNote: Bars website posting or federal database reporting of disputed deficiencies until final dispute determinations are made.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability provisions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department rulemaking under chapter 536 and establishes statutory nonseverability clauses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.545 governing Missouri Informal Dispute Resolution Act procedures, third-party conferences, and rules.

headings.title: Title citation as Authorized Electronic Monitoring Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 198.610 to 198.632 as the Authorized Electronic Monitoring in Long-Term Care Facilities Act.

headings.title: Definitions under Authorized Electronic Monitoring Act
headings.reviewNote: Defines authorized electronic monitoring, department, electronic monitoring device, facility, and resident.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.610 establishing the Authorized Electronic Monitoring Act title and statutory definitions.

headings.title: Resident right to install electronic monitoring device
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees facility residents the right to install and operate authorized electronic monitoring devices in their rooms.

headings.title: Facility immunity from civil and criminal liability
headings.reviewNote: Grants facilities immunity from liability arising from resident use or disclosure of electronic monitoring recordings.

headings.title: Immunity from HIPAA and privacy violation claims
headings.reviewNote: Protects facilities from civil and criminal HIPAA or privacy liability resulting from authorized electronic monitoring.

headings.title: Restrictions on releasing monitoring footage and exception
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits releasing recordings without written resident and facility permission, excepting abuse or neglect cases.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority for electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate administrative rules pursuant to chapter 536 to implement monitoring provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.612 governing resident rights to monitor, facility immunity, footage releases, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Criteria establishing unauthorized electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Defines unauthorized monitoring as placement that is not open and obvious or lacks required facility notifications.

headings.title: Facility and department immunity for unauthorized devices
headings.reviewNote: Grants facilities and the department civil immunity regarding unauthorized placement or use of electronic monitoring devices.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.614 governing definition of unauthorized electronic monitoring and facility civil immunity.

headings.title: Resident sole authority to request monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Provides that competent residents possess sole authority to request electronic monitoring, superseding powers of attorney.

headings.title: Guardian authority to request electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes appointed guardians to request monitoring when residents have been judicially declared incapacitated.

headings.title: Legal representative request upon medical incapacity determination
headings.reviewNote: Permits legal representatives to request monitoring when physicians determine residents lack capacity without judicial adjudication.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.618 governing resident capacity to request monitoring, guardian authority, and legal representatives.

headings.title: Submission of prescribed electronic monitoring request form
headings.reviewNote: Requires residents or representatives to submit written requests on department-prescribed forms before installing devices.

headings.title: Required form disclosures, releases, and roommate consent
headings.reviewNote: Requires the request form to release the facility from civil privacy liability, specify whether a video camera will be obstructed in specified circumstances, and obtain roommate consent on a prescribed form.

headings.title: Authority to execute roommate consent for monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Specifies who may execute roommate consent, including roommates, guardians, or authorized legal representatives.

headings.title: Roommate consent form and facility liability release
headings.reviewNote: Requires roommate consent forms to include liability releases protecting facilities from privacy violation claims.

headings.title: Roommate conditional consent and camera pointing restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Allows roommates to condition consent on cameras being pointed away or audio recording being deactivated.

headings.title: Cessation of monitoring upon admission of new roommate
headings.reviewNote: Directs electronic monitoring to cease immediately when new roommates move in until their written consent is obtained.

headings.title: Department authority to prescribe form contents
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to include additional appropriate consumer protections and guidance on prescribed forms.

headings.title: Recordkeeping rules for executed electronic monitoring forms
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to adopt rules governing where and how long executed monitoring forms must be maintained.

headings.title: Prerequisites for device installation and operation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits commencing monitoring or installing a device until all request and consent forms are returned, and requires compliance with roommate consent conditions and fixed-position installation.

headings.title: Facility right of access to monitoring footage
headings.reviewNote: Grants facilities the right to access and copy all monitoring footage at the facility's expense.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked editorial subsection headings for section 198.620 governing request forms, roommate consent, liability releases, and facility footage access.

headings.title: Facility duty to permit authorized electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Requires long-term care facilities to permit residents or representatives to conduct authorized electronic monitoring.

headings.title: Mandatory posted notice at resident room entrance
headings.reviewNote: Requires posting and maintaining conspicuous notices at room entrances stating electronic monitoring is conducted.

headings.title: Voluntary and noncompulsory nature of electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that electronic monitoring is voluntary and shall not be compulsory for any facility resident.

headings.title: Prohibition against discrimination or retaliation by facility
headings.reviewNote: Bars facilities from refusing admission or removing residents because of electronic monitoring requests or activities.

headings.title: Facility duty to make reasonable physical accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to make reasonable accommodations, including secure mounting locations and electrical power.

headings.title: Resident responsibility for installation and device costs
